chapters.summary: Father Eric Cruz delivers an invocation invoking the Statue of Liberty's words, blessing council members, and calling on them to serve the homeless, immigrants, and vulnerable New Yorkers with justice and compassion.
chapters.title: Invocation by Father Eric Cruz of Church of St. Anselm and St. Roch

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now have today's invocation, which will be delivered by Father Eric Cruz of the Church of St.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Anselm and St.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Rock, which is located at 685 Tintin Avenue in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: You inspired centuries ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: The great words inscribed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: On the Statue of Liberty in this harbor, give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Almighty God of Jesus Christ, Abraham, and Muhammad, you have woven together men and women of various gifts and talents into a rich tapestry of cultures, languages, creeds, and experiences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: A living tapestry that gathers beneath this dome in this hall of justice to exercise a sacred calling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Public service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: They carry the weight of the hopes and aspirations as well as the needs, concerns, and challenges of every person in this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: While the task is great, not greater than the grace and power of your Holy Spirit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: The spirit of love, compassion, wisdom that will occupy this space and inspire our hearts to walk in your way, the way of justice and peace.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Bless these members of the city council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Open your eyes and our hearts to see ourselves as one of the least.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: A homeless grandmother, a jobless father,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: used migrant, a child thirsting for food, medication, and love.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Give these members the strength and fortitude to oppose the vast forces of division and oppression.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Grant courage and conviction to protect, save, and welcome innocent lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: From far distant shores that have traveled a trail of tears seeking new life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Grant your mercy and compassion, your guidance, as they discuss, create, and strive to pass bills and laws that direct and govern our very lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: To feed the hungry, grant shelter to the homeless, and certainly foster humanity and dignity to those in dire need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: These members, your children, in accepting this great task are not in service to themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: They are in service to truth, justice, and true charity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Lord, you remind us that we are our brother's keeper, our sister's keeper.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: You remind us of a higher calling, and most particular to the City Council, the calling of public service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Service that they are pleased and willing to accept.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Raising the honor and dignity of every person in this city to continue to become and be a light of hope and dreams and new life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Father Eric Cruz
utterances.text: Amen.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Member Elsie Encarnación moves to spread the invocation in full on the record, praising Father Cruz's ministry in the South Bronx and highlighting the St. Anselm affordable housing apartments that brought hundreds of affordable homes to the community.
chapters.title: Council Member Encarnación spreads invocation on record and honors Father Cruz

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I would now ask Councilmember Elsie Encarnación to spread the invocation on the record.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I've had the privilege of knowing Father Eric Cruz through his work across the Bronx, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to recognize him today following that powerful invocation.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Father Cruz has spent his ministry serving the South Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: From his early work at Bronx Lebanon Hospital to his pastoral leadership at parishes across our borough.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Today, as pastor of St.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Anselm and Rock in Mount Haven, Father Cruz continues that tradition of service, and we've seen and felt the impact of your work firsthand in District 8.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The new St.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Anselm apartments on Tintin Avenue have brought hundreds of affordable homes to our community along with on-site supportive services like case management, legal and medical referrals, counseling, and employment assistance.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: That kind of housing.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: is especially important in a borough where affordable rent is scarce and where too many of our neighbors with disabilities or histories of homelessness are left without a safe place to land.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And what makes this project so meaningful is how it came together.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Catholic Charities, the Archdiocese, and Father Cruz saw an opportunity to turn a parking lot into a home for our neighbors, and you did it.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: While this is a power example of what is possible when faith-based organizations, government, and our communities come together

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: around a shared commitment to housing and dignity, this is exactly the kind of innovative, faith-rooted partnership that the South Bronx needs.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I would like to thank you, Father Eric Cruz, for being here today.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I want to make a motion for unanimous consent to spread the invocation in full upon the record.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin announces that council employee Rafael Rubio has been granted permanent asylum after being wrongfully detained by ICE in January and placed in solitary confinement. She notes the council's $82 million allocation for immigration legal services.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Council employee Rafael Rubio granted permanent asylum

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Happy August.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It has been not a slow August, a very busy August.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I want to start off with some absolutely incredible news.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our amazing City Council employee, Rafael Rubio, has been granted permanent asylum.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is such an incredible victory.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We were involved with his case since he was wrongfully detained by ICE back in January.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And just knowing now that he finally has permanent asylum is really, really incredible.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: He can finally breathe a sigh of relief knowing that he can continue to live and work right here where he belongs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I do just want to say that the fight for him ended in justice, but he was wrongfully detained.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: He was put in solitary confinement for two weeks during that detainment.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I really want to commend Rafael.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: He has such an incredible spirit.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: He was positive throughout this ordeal he went through, and we couldn't be happier that he is home.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I do want to say that for many other New Yorkers, they are not getting the same outcome that Rafael did, and that is why we will continue to fight for them.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: That is why we fought so hard to have close to $82 million allocated in the budget for immigration legal services.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: support them.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin condemns the Trump administration's decision to end Temporary Protected Status for Haitian immigrants, stripping work permits and leaving them vulnerable to deportation. She names council members Narcisse, Joseph, Louis, and Ossé as mobilizing to assist Haitian New Yorkers.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Trump administration ends TPS for Haitian immigrants

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Last week, the Trump administration announced that they would be ending temporary protected status for Haitian immigrants, stripping them of work permits and leaving them vulnerable to deportation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is a tremendous injustice, not only for those whose livelihoods are in limbo, for their family members and for our entire city who relies on their countless contributions.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I want to say that the council stands in solidarity with council members Mercedes Narcisse, Councilmember Rita Joseph, Councilmember Farrah Lewis, and Councilmember Chi-A.-Ossé,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: who represent our Haitian New York community and who are mobilizing to assist our Haitian neighbors through legal access and Know Your Rights campaigns, as is the City Council.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin addresses the expiration of federal funding for legal aid for immigrant children, praises Governor Hochul's announcement of $7 million in state funding for unaccompanied minors, and reaffirms New York's commitment to immigrant neighbors.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: State funding for unaccompanied minors legal aid

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The administration is also abandoning our most vulnerable immigrants, our children, having let federal funding for legal aid expire at the end of July.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But New York will not sit idly by.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yesterday, Governor Hochul announced that the state will provide more than $7 million to legal aid services supporting unaccompanied minors, and I applaud her for the action that she's taken.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Every person has a right to representation, including and particularly a child without their parents, and it's unconscionable to think otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The government's commitment also bolsters the council's funding that supports various legal agencies that work with immigrants.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So from City Hall to Albany, New York.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: continues to stand by our immigrant neighbors, and we are always a resource for all people in need.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin announces she sent letters to Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, and Gemini launching an investigation into predatory marketing practices targeting minors on prediction market platforms, with 60 questions for each company.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Investigation launched into prediction market platforms

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Another avenue, on a different note, that we are pursuing to protect New Yorkers revolves around predatory marketing practices.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: After months of examining allegations of these practices across prediction market industry,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I sent letters to four platforms, Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, and Gemini, notifying them that the council is beginning an investigation against them.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: For any of you that have been on these sites, You can see, and this is what we are alleging, that there are predatory marketing practices that are really focused on minors,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: focused on minors and luring them in to the gambling that is occurring on these platforms.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So the next generation of New Yorkers is increasingly targeted by the prediction market industry's aggressive advertising tactics.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our letter has 60 questions for these four companies, and our goal is to determine whether additional laws, funding, or programs are needed to protect them if the allegations indeed prove to be true.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I will just say, as a mother, what they're doing is concerning, and as a former commissioner of the Department of Consumer Affairs, this is something that I think is a really important consumer protection issue that we need to take very seriously.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Not only do we have the ability, but I would argue we have an obligation to harness the full weight of the

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: of this city council to protect minors from practices that appear to be aimed at them.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin announces the Scoop Act package, which will expand access to dog waste bags, launch a composting pilot program for dog runs, establish a public education campaign, and strengthen enforcement of dog waste rules.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Scoop Act to expand dog waste management

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Shifting gears towards today's legislation, and perhaps on a slightly lighter note, we are so excited to pass the Scoop Act today.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This package of bills will expand access to dog waste bags, launch a pilot program to compost waste collected from dog runs, establish a public education campaign, and strengthen our enforcement of these rules.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is about creating safer and cleaner streets and parks for residents and furry friends alike.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin details rising insurance costs: homeowners insurance up 26% annually, liability insurance up 10%, small businesses paying 4-5 times the national average, and auto insurance 52% higher than other states. She announces an investigation into insurance pricing.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Rising insurance costs burdening New Yorkers and small businesses

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So whether or not you own a dog, one quality of life issue that affects all New Yorkers is, of course, affordability.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And one factor driving this crisis is rising insurance costs, costs that are some of the highest in the country.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Homeowners insurance in New York has been increasing by 26% annually.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Liability insurance across all industries in New York has been increasing by 10% annually.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If you're a small business in New York, you will be paying four to five times the national average on liability insurance.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If you own a car in New York,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Auto insurance for New Yorkers is around 52% higher than in other states.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: These costs pose enormous burdens on New Yorkers, but small businesses in particular.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And for many small businesses are forced.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to raise their prices or go out of business because of the high cost of insurance.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's no wonder that our city lost 8,000 businesses in the second quarter of 2025 alone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our office will investigate why insurance prices are so high so that we can take steps to lower them.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We'll engage insurers, stakeholders, and regulators so we know exactly what actions we need to take moving forward.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are determined to create a livable city.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: For all and that means an affordable city for all as well.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin announces a package of bills allowing sidewalk cafes to operate 365 days a year, providing vital revenue for restaurants while addressing sanitation concerns including debris, trash, and rats.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Outdoor dining package allowing year-round operation

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As summer comes to close, I'm sure the last thing we want on our minds is the winter months, but let's face it, restaurant owners are always looking ahead and we in the City Council are looking out for them too.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are passing today a package of bills on outdoor dining, which would allow sidewalk cafes to operate 365 days a year.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And for many restaurants, that ability to serve customers outside all year round would provide vital, vital revenue.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As a former restaurant owner myself, I know that every single dollar counts, especially in the midst of an affordability crisis.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: At the same time, we want to balance the comments and concerns we've heard from communities across our city to ensure that any kind of sidewalk cafe

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: or roadway dining is kept free of debris, of trash, of rats.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And so a number of bills in this package really address some of those.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: sanitation issues as well, and I think this really strikes a proper balance.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Who turned, I just want to say this, he turned 32.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin recognizes National Black Business Month, Women's Equality Day on August 26, and multiple Independence Days including Jamaican, Ecuadorian, Pakistani, Indian, Ukrainian, and Trinidad and Tobago.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: August recognitions including Black Business Month, Women's Equality Day, and Independence Days

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So throughout the month of August, we have many important holidays and events to recognize.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: August is National Black Business Month.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Black New Yorkers own and operate so many important businesses across our city, but they still face longstanding inequities.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm proud of the work that the council has done to cut red tape for business owners so that everyone

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: can afford to live here, stay here, and achieve the American dream.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: August 26th is Women's Equality Day, commemorating the anniversary of women's suffrage being added to our Constitution 106 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm thankful for the advocacy of former New York Congresswoman Bella Abzug, who put this day on the calendar, and countless other women who paved the way for generations of women to come.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As a woman majority council, we benefit from their efforts each and every day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: There's a lot of Independence Days to celebrate.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I'm going to be announcing a few of them.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: August 6th was Jamaican Independence Day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: August 10th was Ecuadorian Independence Day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Tomorrow is Pakistani Independence Day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Saturday is Indian Independence Day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: August 24th is Ukrainian Independence Day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And August 31st is the Independence Day of Trinidad and Tobago.

chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Farewell to Parliamentarian Jeff Campagna

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And finally, I really want to shout out our parliamentarian, Jeff Campagna, who is sadly leaving the council.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we really just want to thank you for all of your incredible contributions, your professionalism, your dedication, and we wish you well on this next chapter and journey.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you, Jeff.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin outlines four land use items: 50-20 108th Street rezoning (196 units, 51 affordable), 6302 Fresh Pond Road rezoning (54 units, 13 affordable), Queens CD2 Walk to Park site selection, and Flatiron Nomad Major Concessions expansion.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Land use items overview including rezonings and park site selection

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And now we're going to move on to our stated agenda.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have a long agenda, everyone, so just bear with me here.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: First, we're going to vote on the following land use items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 50-20 108th Street rezoning will facilitate the development of two new mixed-use buildings with 196 dwelling units, 51 of which will be permanently affordable under MIH Option 1 in Councilmember Thomas Henry's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The Council is modifying this application to strike MIH Option 2 and to reduce the rezoning area to preserve existing small homes that are not within the proposed development.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 6302 Fresh Pond Road rezoning will enable the development of a new seven-story mixed-use building with 54 dwelling units, 13 of which will be permanently affordable under MIH Option 1 in Councilmember Wong's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The Council is modifying this application to strike MIH Option 2.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Queen's CD2 Walk to Park Site Selection will facilitate the site selection and potential acquisition of 31

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: privately owned properties by the Department of Parks in collaboration with the Department of Citywide Administrative Services as part of a citywide plan to support a more

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: equitable distribution of open space.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: These acquisitions will facilitate the creation of new parkland in the districts of Council Members Krishnan and Wan.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Flatiron Nomad Major Concessions will improve the expansion of the existing Flatiron District concession area boundaries in the districts of Council Members Wilson and Epstein.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin outlines two finance items: a transparency resolution approving new designations for expense budget funding, and a preconsidered introduction by Council Member Linda Lee to establish a temporary program resolving outstanding ECB judgment penalties.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Finance items overview including transparency resolution and ECB judgments

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We will also be voting on the following finance items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: A transparency resolution approving new designations and changes of certain organizations receiving funding in the expense budget.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: A pre-considered introduction sponsored by Councilmember Linda Lee will require the Department of Finance Commissioner to establish a temporary program to resolve outstanding ECB judgment penalties.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Resolution 218 by Council Member Hudson declaring August 2 as James Baldwin Day, and Introduction 839A by Council Member Pierina Sanchez making the Certification of No Harassment pilot program permanent.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: James Baldwin Day resolution and Certification of No Harassment overview

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, we'll also vote on the following pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 218, sponsored by Councilmember Crystal Hudson, would declare August 2nd annually as James Baldwin Day in the City of New York to honor his legacy as a groundbreaking essayist, novelist, playwright,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: poet, and civil rights activist who fought racial and sexual discrimination with candor, sensitivity, and lasting influence.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to our staff, YM Diuri and Jessica Boulay.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 839A, sponsored by Councilmember Pierina-Ana-Sanchez, would make the certification of no harassment pilot program permanent with a new program list published by the Department of

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: housing preservation and development every three years beginning on April 15th, 2027.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Elliot Heisler, Austin Malone, Dirk Spencer, William Eck, and Jose Conde.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Introduction 320A by Council Member Frank Morano, which would codify the current flag of the borough of Staten Island as its official flag into city law.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Staten Island flag codification overview

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 320A, sponsored by Councilmember Frank Marano, would codify into law the current flag of the borough of Staten Island as its official flag.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Jahari Frazier and Erica Cohen.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Resolution 395 (homeowners insurance rate cap), Resolution 389 (auto insurance consumer information), Resolution 387 (property insurance for affordable housing), and Introduction 685B establishing an Office of Insurance Affordability.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Insurance resolutions and Office of Insurance Affordability overview

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 395, sponsored also by Councilmember Frank Marano, would call on the New York State Legislature to pass and the governor to sign

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: S6356A4188, prohibiting increasing in rates of homeowners insurance in excess of 25%.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Natalie Meltzer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 389, sponsored by Councilmember Eric-Dinowitz, will call on the New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign the Automobile Insurance Consumer Information Act.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Natalie Meltzer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 387, sponsored by Councilmember Gail Brewer, will call on the New York State Legislature

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to pass and the Governor to sign A07828A, S07939, A9015, and A9016A to mitigate the rising cost of property insurance for affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Madeline Meltzer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 685B, sponsored by myself, would establish an office.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: of insurance accountability to support consumers navigating the insurance market and address the rising cost of insurance.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Sarah Swain and Natalie Meltzer.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews four dog waste bills: Intro 872 (public education campaign by Hanif), Intro 864 (composting pilot by Epstein), Intro 880 (park signage by Narcisse), and Intro 857A (dog waste bag dispensers on 1,200 litter baskets).
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Scoop Act dog waste bills overview

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 872, sponsored by Councilmember Shahana Hanif, would require the Commissioner of DOHMH, in consultation with the Commissioner of Sanitation, to develop and conduct a public education and outreach campaign

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to inform the public about dog waste removal and the dangers of failing to remove dog waste.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Declan McPherson and Morgan Barrett.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 864, sponsored by Councilmember Epstein, would require the Commissioner of Parks to establish a pilot program to collect dog waste from dog runs under the Department of Parks jurisdiction for composting.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Chris Sartori.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 880, sponsored by Councilmember Narcisse, would require signage at the entrances and exits of parks and at certain park facilities, stating the rule prohibiting a person from leaving dog waste on the ground

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and the associated penalties for violation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Chris Sartori.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 857A would require the Department of Sanitation to install and regularly fill dog waste bag dispensers on or next to no less than 1,200 public litter baskets on city streets.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Morgan Barrett.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Introduction 935A by Council Member Feliz, requiring NYPD to report quarterly on confirmed firearm discharges including date, time, location, and circumstances.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Firearm discharge reporting bill overview

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 935A.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Sponsored by Councilmember Feliz would require the NYPD to report on the number of confirmed firearm discharges in the city on a quarterly basis.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The NYPD would be required to report the date, time, and location of each firearm discharge, as well as a description of the circumstances surrounding the discharge.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Josh Kingsley and Chad Benjamin.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews four outdoor dining bills: Intro 655A (year-round roadway cafes by Restler), Intro 895A (sidewalk cafe enclosures by Brewer), Intro 917A (sanitation requirements by Justin Sanchez), and Intro 918A (quarterly fee installments by Thomas-Henry).
chapters.title: Speaker Menin: Outdoor dining bills overview

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 655A, sponsored by Councilmember Lincoln-Restler, would expand the city's outdoor dining program by removing seasonal restrictions on roadway cafe operation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This bill would also allow the use of weatherproofing and winterizing materials to facilitate the operation of a roadway cafe year-round.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Rachel Codrera, Sarah Swain, and Natalie Meltzer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 895A, sponsored by Councilmember Gail Brewer, would allow sidewalk cafe operators to enclose their year-round sidewalk cafes annually from November 30th to March 31st.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This bill also permits weather protection materials that may be used at other times during the year.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Rachel Codrero, Sarah Swain, and Natalie Meltzer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 917A, sponsored by Councilmember Justin Sanchez, would require roadway

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and sidewalk cafe operators to ensure that their outdoor setups are clear of trash, debris, graffiti, vermin, food scraps, and unsanitary conditions.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Operators who violate this...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: will be subject to civil penalties.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Rachel Codrera, Sarah Swain, and Natalie Meltzer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And then finally, last but certainly not least, Introduction 918A, sponsored by Councilmember Shanel-Thomas-Henry,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: would allow sidewalk and roadway cafe operators to pay their annual revocable consent fees and quarterly installments to reduce their upfront costs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Rachel Codrera, Sarah Swain, and Natalie Meltzer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm going to turn it back to our Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I want to remind folks that because we are voting on transparency resolutions, it would be great if before the vote you can make your disclosure.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now move into discussion of general orders, beginning with Councilmember Carl Wilson, followed by Epstein.

chapters.summary: Council Member Carl Wilson speaks in support of the Flatiron Nomad Major Concessions agreement, highlighting the BID's stewardship of the Broadway corridor, expanded revenue for public spaces, cleaning services, compost bins, and potential public bathrooms. He thanks Council Member Epstein and council land use staff.
chapters.title: Council Member Wilson on Flatiron Nomad Major Concessions agreement

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Since its genesis 20 years ago, the Flatiron Nomad Partnership has been an excellent steward of the area now extending from the Flatiron to all of Nomad and 20th Street and 6th Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: The Broadway Corridor, one of the most high traffic areas of the city, grew exponentially in a post-pandemic world as demand for outdoor dining, public space activation, and pedestrianized streets amplified.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Flatiron Nomad met and exceeded all expectations of what it could do for the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: So I hope my colleagues will join me today in supporting the Flatiron Nomads'promising next chapter with this major concession agreement.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: This agreement will significantly expand the ways the bid can generate revenue that will lead to more beautiful public spaces, expanded cleaning services for the district, and additional smart compost bins.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: It also unlocks the future potential for the installation of public bathrooms and water fountains.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I'm eager to see the ways this agreement transforms our neighborhood for the better.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I really want to thank Councilmember Harvey Epstein for his partnership and for taking the lead in getting this process started while the council seat in District 3 was vacant.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And thank you to the bid for all they do to keep our communities beautiful, safe, and prosperous.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And a big thank you to DOT and DSNY for their collaboration and willingness to think constructively about how we can maximize our ability to invest in our public spaces.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And I also want to shout out the council land use team.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: who was critical during this whole process, Omar, Chelsea, Arthur, Anne, and Dana, and especially Dana, for supporting this effort, and to my chief of staff, Hannah Moses, as well as the rest of my team for their hard work.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: It's my hope that the partnership can continue its work preserving and beautifying the landscape along Broadway and beyond, and that we can be a meaningful companion in that endeavor.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Epstein, followed by Thomas Henry.

chapters.summary: Council Member Epstein thanks Wilson for partnership on the Flatiron Nomad concession, praising commitments for water fountains, public restrooms, and compost bins. He also thanks the Speaker for the Scoop Act and highlights his dog waste composting bill, and thanks the council for pet food pantry budget allocations.
chapters.title: Council Member Epstein on Flatiron Nomad concessions and Scoop Act composting

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I also want to thank Councilmember Wilson for his friendship and partnership during this major concession.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I think probably on day two when he started, he was like, Mike Carl, we have to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Deal with it quickly.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And really, the planning and land use staff and the Flatiron Nomad partnership was amazing.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Our staff, Dana and Chelsea, really helped us get through this process.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And a major concession agreement is really to make sure that the Broadway space is managed by this bid,

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: but also talks about things we care deeply about, about sustainability, public access to space, securing commitments for water fountains, public restrooms, compostable bins, and waste removal.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This is like a comprehensive plan that I'm really proud of.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I also want to thank the speaker for the SCOOP Act.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This issue came up early in her term.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I saw what was happening during the winter and then all the dog waste, and she kind of, she jumped right on it.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We created a package, allowed the Animal Caucus to take some leadership in this, and, you know, the bill that I'm talking about on composting dog waste is both an environment

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: issue and a cleanliness issue and I think this all across the board is really really palatable for the future of New York and a plan that we can really be proud of.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And finally I just I know we're talking about some budget allocations I don't have conflicts but I really want to thank the council for allocating what we did in the budget on pet food pantries we're making some of those allocations today I think that's going to help the affordability crisis we're seeing in New York.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I know we keep talking about affordability and I know the leadership of the speaker and this council we're actually acting on those issues and are moving those issues forward today.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Thomas Henry, followed by Pierina Sanchez.

chapters.summary: Council Member Thomas-Henry speaks about her first bill to pass, Intro 918, which allows outdoor dining operators to pay revocable consent fees in quarterly installments instead of upfront, easing the financial burden on small business owners.
chapters.title: Council Member Thomas-Henry on outdoor dining fee installment bill

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Our communities are changing, and as New York continues to grow, we have to be intentional about making sure the people and businesses that gave our neighborhoods their identity can afford to be part of what comes next.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Because when you think about small businesses in New York, you think about the restaurant owner who takes a family recipe and turns it into a neighborhood favorite.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The immigrant entrepreneur who opens a storefront and creates a piece of home a thousand miles away.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Or the New Yorker who saves every dollar they can, takes a chance on themselves, signs a lease, turns on the lights, and says, I'm going to make this work.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: That is the culture of entrepreneurship in New York.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Before I ever sat in this chamber, I was a small business owner.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So I know there is nothing small about running a business in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: It takes courage.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: to bet on yourself.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: It takes grit to open those doors every morning, make payroll, pay the rent, navigate regulations, serve your customers, and take care of your family, and somehow wake up the next morning ready to do it all again.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So when government has an opportunity to make that journey a little easier, we should.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Today I am incredibly proud that the council will vote on Intro 918, my first bill to pass this body.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The bill is simple.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Instead of requiring restaurants participating in outdoor dining to pay revocable consent fees all at once, they will have the flexibility to pay quarterly.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Because the difference between one enormous bill and manageable payments throughout the year matters.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And this is bigger than outdoor dining.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: It is about asking ourselves, who gets to stay, who gets to build, and who gets to be a part of the future of New York City?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Affordability isn't only about what it costs to live here.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: It is about what it costs to build a life, build a business, and chase a dream here.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Our entrepreneurs make New York the New York we love.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The least we can do is meet them where they are and make it a little easier for them to build their dreams here.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I'm proud that today this council is doing exactly that.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Pierina-Sanchez, followed by Ressler.

chapters.summary: Council Member Pierina Sanchez speaks on Intro 839A, making the Certification of No Harassment program permanent and stronger by expanding harassment definitions to include ICE threats, monitoring problematic portfolios, and strengthening violation clearance incentives.
chapters.title: Council Member Pierina Sanchez on permanent Certification of No Harassment program

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader, and thank you to my 30 colleagues who have co-sponsored the certification of no harassment bill today.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Every tenant in New York City deserves to live free from harassment, regardless of their

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: citizenship status.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Yet we are in a moment where the federal government is targeting immigrant communities, and we must ensure that all of our neighbors receive the strongest possible protections in their homes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, the council will vote on 839A, legislation that will bring the certification of no harassment program, will make it permanent and stronger.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: CONH was first created in 2018 to deter owners from using construction to harass and displace tenants from their homes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: After two successful pilots, CONH has proven itself to be useful for identifying high-risk buildings and deterring bad behavior.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, we build on that success and codify CONH as a permanent tool in the city by doing three things.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: First, responding to rising reports of landlords threatening to call ICE on their tenants by expanding the definition of harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Second, monitoring problematic portfolios by reviewing all buildings that have the same owner as those with finding of harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And third, create a stronger incentive to clear violations, allowing buildings to exit the program only if owners significantly improve living conditions for their tenants.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, this bill will clarify that the basic maintenance continues to be allowed without delay for any building in the program, which has been a point of misinformation during this debate.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And to close, I just want to thank my team, the Coalition of Advocates who made this possible, and the agencies.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: But just very particularly want to thank our Deputy Chief of Staff, Ben Ratner, and our legislative fellow, Dylan Campos, who really took this on as their legislative baby, as I keep saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: and really made this happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: So thank you, congratulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: And holler back at my team who's in the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Ressler, followed by Narcisse.

chapters.summary: Council Member Restler discusses the outdoor dining legislation, noting the 90% decline in restaurants offering outdoor dining after Adams-era reforms. He highlights year-round operation, design enhancements, modified operating hours, accountability metrics, and thanks Speaker Menin and staff.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler on restoring year-round outdoor dining

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It was about three years ago that the Adams era reforms to outdoor dining were approved, and it nearly broke the outdoor dining program.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It led to a 90% decline in restaurants offering outdoor dining across the five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And the number one reason that restaurants stopped offering outdoor dining is because we made it stupidly expensive.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Stupidly expensive to have to construct, to deconstruct, and to store outdoor dining structures.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: For small neighborhood restaurants, it just didn't work.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The most salient benefit, the greatest win in this legislation to restore year-round outdoor dining, is that we anticipate thousands of additional restaurants are going to offer outdoor dining

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: across all of our communities, making this, adding to the vibrancy and dynamism of our neighborhoods, creating jobs.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: On average, whenever a restaurant adds outdoor dining, it creates a new job.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So we have the potential of making a significant impact on our local economy.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We've also incorporated some design enhancements that allow for vertical elements and overhead structures during inclement weather and winter to make it more pleasant to eat outside.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We've modified the timing that outdoor dining structures can operate, allowing them to operate.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: earlier in the morning for coffee establishments, and we've asked them to close earlier in the evening, so they have to shutter their doors by 11 o'clock and send people inside.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: There's also real accountability metrics in this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: If you were issued the same violation three times in a two-year period, then a restaurant's outdoor...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Dining license is revoked, which is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I do recognize that the seasonal program has made enormous strides in improving the cleanliness of outdoor dining.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Last year, there were just 11 311 complaints for outdoor dining relating to garbage, rats, the like.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: This is a really good win, and I'm really grateful for Speaker Menon championing this, and I just want to thank Jonathan from her team, Rachel, Sarah Swain, and my Chief of Staff, Molly, and lots of others.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Council Member Morano speaks on Intro 320, his first bill to pass, codifying the Staten Island flag into city law. He frames it as a message that Staten Island matters and is seen by city government, thanking the Staten Island delegation and flag designer Amal Micah.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I rise today with a great deal of...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: of pride in support of Introduction 320, which will make the Staten Island flag official, officially codified into city law.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Now, I know there are people who will say, it's just a flag.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I respectfully disagree.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: For Staten Islanders, this is about something much larger.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: For too long, many people in my borough have felt that when decisions are made in this building at City Hall, Staten Island is somewhere off in the distance, and not just geographically.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Today sends a different message.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We see you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: City government sees you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Your history matters.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Your identity matters.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You matter.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Your borough matters.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I hope this is part of a new chapter in the relationship between Staten Island and city government.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Today, we're getting our flag recognized.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And tomorrow, hopefully, it's our transportation needs, our infrastructure, our public safety concerns, and all the other things Staten Islanders have been rightly yelling about for years.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We're very grateful for the flag.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We're not going to stop calling 311 with other complaints.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I want to thank Speaker Julie-Menin for her support, all of my colleagues in the council, and especially my partners in the Staten Island Council delegation, Majority Whip Camila Hanks and my brother, Minority Leader David Carr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I want to recognize Amal Micah, whose beautiful design.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Today, Staten Island isn't the forgotten borough.

chapters.summary: Council Member Hanif speaks in support of Intro 872A, her legislation creating a multilingual public education campaign on dog waste removal. She highlights public health risks including E. coli and salmonella, and notes the bill requires effectiveness evaluation using 311 data.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif on dog waste education campaign bill

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Permission to explain my vote.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Permission granted.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Today I speak in support of the SCOOP Act package and Intro 872A, my legislation to create a citywide multilingual education campaign on dog waste.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: First, I want to be clear, I love dogs.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: And because I love dogs and our city, I am proud to support the SCOOP Act.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: We all know New York City has a dog poop problem.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: We've seen it, smelled it, and unfortunately, many of us have stepped in it.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: But this is about more than an unpleasant sidewalk experience.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Dog waste is a public health and environmental issue.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Pet waste can pollute our waterways and carry harmful bacteria and parasites, including E.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Coli, salmonella, and roundworm.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Most New Yorkers know they're supposed to pick up after their dogs, but not everyone understands why it matters or the broader consequences for our neighbors, our streets, and our environment when they don't.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: That's why Intro 872A focuses on education.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: It will make sure New Yorkers understand both their legal obligation to clean up after their pets and the public health and environmental reasons behind it.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: And importantly, that information will be available in multiple languages so we can reach dog owners across the entire city.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: The bill also makes sure we can measure

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: whether our efforts are working.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: It requires an evaluation of the campaign's effectiveness and incorporates 311 data on dog waste complaints.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: That will give us real information to track progress and understand where additional education and outreach may be needed.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon, for her leadership and support, and my colleagues for advancing the SCOOP Act and the staff who worked with us to get Intro 872A to the floor today.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I'm proud to vote yes, and I urge my colleagues to do the same.

chapters.summary: Council Member Hudson speaks on Resolution 218, honoring James Baldwin as a groundbreaking essayist, novelist, playwright, and civil rights activist who fought racial and sexual discrimination. She highlights his legacy of fearless truth-telling as a Black gay man.
chapters.title: Council Member Hudson on James Baldwin Day resolution

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We will now move into discussion of resolutions, beginning with Council Member Hudson, followed by Dinowitz.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Today we're honoring a New Yorker whose words changed the way this country understood itself and challenged us to become something better.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: James Baldwin was born in Harlem 102 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Throughout his life, he never stopped asking this country to live up to its promises of freedom.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: He wrote with extraordinary honesty about race, sexuality, love, faith, and what it means to find your place in a country that so often tells you you do not belong.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Baldwin's legacy is extraordinary not only because of what he wrote, but because of how fearlessly he lived and spoke his truth.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: As a black gay man in a country that routinely denied both his racial and sexual identity, Baldwin refused to make himself smaller to fit within the limits society placed on him.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: He understood that telling the truth, especially when that truth makes people uncomfortable, can itself be an act of resistance.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: He once wrote, not everything that is faced can be changed, but nothing can be changed until it is faced.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: That idea is at the heart of Baldwin's work.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: His belief in our capacity to change is part of what makes Baldwin's legacy so revolutionary.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Nearly four decades after his death, his words still resonate.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: They still challenge us to confront injustice and question the systems around us.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: For hardworking New Yorkers.

utterances.text: It is nearly twice the national average.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Now the New York State Department of Financial Services regulates automobile insurance.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz

utterances.text: This bill would authorize

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz

chapters.summary: Council Member Morano speaks on Resolution 395, his first resolution, urging Albany to prohibit homeowners insurance rate increases exceeding 25% per year. He notes average premiums rose over $1,000 since 2020 and nearly half a million NYC homeowners are uninsured.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: This is the first resolution of mine that I hope will pass the New York City Council, and I really couldn't be prouder that it's won.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: One aimed squarely at helping homeowners and making this city a little bit more affordable.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Wherever we fall on the political spectrum, affordability is a key word.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I want to thank the Speaker for her leadership and support and the committee for advancing this resolution and the entire council for supporting it.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Since 2020, New York homeowners have seen average insurance premiums rise by more than $1,000.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Nearly half a million New York homeowners are completely uninsured, and that's an affordability crisis hiding in plain sight.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And this resolution simply urges Albany to pass a bill which would prohibit homeowners'insurance rates increasing more than 25% in a single year, except when otherwise agreed to in the policy.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Let's put that in perspective.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: 25% is still a pretty generous definition of relief.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If Con Ed announced a 25% increase tomorrow, we'd probably have three hearings and a press conference a day.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you for your support.

chapters.summary: Council Member Won introduces a resolution with Public Advocate Williams calling for Daniel's Law, ensuring localities have plans for mental health crisis response. She notes NYPD officers have fatally shot at least 20 individuals in mental health crises in eight years.
chapters.title: Council Member Won on Daniel's Law mental health crisis response

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Councilmember Wilson, followed by Hanif.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: I am honored to introduce, in collaboration with public advocate Jumaane Williams, a resolution calling on the New York State Legislature to pass and the governor to sign Daniel's Law.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Daniel's Law would ensure that every locality in our state has a plan and resources in place for responding to mental health-related emergencies in a sensitive, constructive manner informed by modern advances in and understandings of mental health care.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: When worried families seek support for a loved one undergoing a mental health crisis, they hope that person will be treated with care and dignity.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Unfortunately, too often, the tragedy deepens from there.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: According to the Mayor's Office of Community Mental Health, in the past eight years, NYPD officers have fatally shot at least 20 individuals experiencing a mental health crisis.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: There has to be a better, more humane way to respond to our loved ones in crisis.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Daniel's Law will ensure compassionate crisis response in every community, as well as a focus on preventative mental health care.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Member Narcisse urges colleagues not to ignore the Haitian community's suffering after TPS termination, noting they were invited legally. She calls for support of S-4814 in the Senate and thanks the Speaker and mayor for addressing the issue.
chapters.title: Council Member Narcisse on Haitian community TPS crisis

utterances.text: Councilmember Narcisse, followed by Marano.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Today, I just want to let everyone know that what's going on with the Haitian community

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Please don't ignore what's going on right now because the world turned and things happen.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: The Haitian community, all I can say for them to stay strong.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I'm not worried about them really to be strong because they've been through it.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: They have seen it.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: They read the books.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: But for all my colleagues, everyone that support the Haitian community,

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So please know that they are going to a tough time in the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And I have to start by saying thank you to Madam Speaker and, of course, the mayor that's talking about it, understanding that we cannot ignore what's going on around us.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And there is one hope that's staying still that opened our head that we can do something about it is S-4814.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: That's in the Senate right now.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: The House did their part.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I want to know from our perspective how the best way we can help the community that's suffering.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: They are suffering for real right in our backyard as well.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And I'm going to continue saying thank you to everyone that understands what's going on when it comes to folks in...

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Sometimes it's not only for the immigration, immigration reform, let me tell you honestly, yes, you can do it, but those folks were here legally, they were invited.

utterances.text: Yes, I'm hearing a lot of people say, oh, well, it's supposed to be temporarily, but honestly, there's a lot of things in our lives that's supposed to be temporarily, but still with us, including all the advantages that we're taking from social

utterances.text: and Medicare and all of that.

utterances.text: So having said that,

utterances.text: We cannot ignore folks that are suffering, children that are separating from their families.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: hang over our head for decades to come.
